addresses.name: CAIUnit_FillGarrisons
addresses.signature: bool __stdcall CAIUnit_FillGarrisons(CAIUnit* agent, void* garrisonDivisions, CList* garrisonTargets, int garrisonCount)
addresses.comment: 0x4CACB0 to the `ret 0x10` at 0x4CB7FD. Candidates are the garrison divisions, plus - when the agent's country is the one played - every division of it with no agent above it. CAIUnit::CountUnitsAtPositions(candidates, targets, any land unit, no allies). Each target in list order wants |garrisonDivisions| / |targets|, the first remainder ones one more; a threatened province (+0x1DC) adds the brigades of the hostile land units heading into it (CollectUnitsMovingIntoProvince with enemiesOnly); the want is held to the stack cap, round(0.5 / (-BASE_STACKING_PENALTY)) (20 where that is not above nought). While have < want: the candidate not in a battle, not retreating, free to leave (UnitMayLeave strict), standing or heading in the target's area (or anywhere, where the target's area is one of the focus areas +0x338), not already there, not in a threatened province, and - unless the target is threatened - not taken from a hold position whose standing less one (none where that position scores less or the target is a depot) is no more than the target's have plus one for a non-depot, nearest by squared map distance (x 2 for an army of role 5 leaving a higher-scored position) and able to reach it, is moved there (MoveUnit 0, 1, 1). The name is ours. **Read again on the listing, 2026-11-10, with the candidate test in full.** Each target wants the number of garrison divisions (the vector, not the split's count) over the targets. A candidate is judged by where it is bound, or where it stands with no destination: that province must be in the target's area (or the target's area a focus area), not the target, not held by a country it is at war with or by the rebels or under an undeclared war, and not threatened. Unless the target is threatened, where that province is itself a target of this list with a score above nought: it is passed over when have(target) + (1, none at a depot) >= standing(there) - (1, none where the target scores more or is a depot). The distance is squared x 16 in single precision, doubled for an army of role 5 where that province scores more than the target (and the target is not threatened); least first, a tie to the earlier unit, and only one that can reach the target. The pick takes one off have where it was bound for a target, or off have and standing where it stood in one with no destination; it is counted as sent whatever MoveUnit answers. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 13.

addresses.name: CAIUnit::CountUnitsAtPositions
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CAIUnit::CountUnitsAtPositions(CAIUnit* this, void* units, CList* records, bool anyLandUnit, bool withAllies)
addresses.comment: Fills a position list's have (+0x10) and standing (+0x14). 0x4D9E30, two `ret 0x10`. For each land unit of the vector (divisions only unless anyLandUnit), not retreating or retreating with an organisation share >= 0.5: the records are walked in list order - the first that is its province counts it standing and heading (have and standing +1) unless it is bound for a province not held by an enemy, when it is counted nowhere; the first that is its destination (GetMovementDestinationProvince) counts it heading. With withAllies, focus areas (+0x340 > 0) and the frontier at war, it recurses over the whole unit list of every non-hostile country other than us that controls a focus area's first province. Callers: CAIUnit_FillLinePositions, CAIUnit_FillGarrisons, CAIUnit_PlaceReserves and itself. The name is ours. Who passes what, on the listing (2026-11-10): CAIUnit_FillLinePositions passes +0x12C, every committed division **garrisons included**, divisions only, with allies; CAIUnit_FillGarrisons its garrison divisions and any land unit, no allies; CAIUnit_PlaceReserves +0x15C, any land unit, no allies. A unit standing in a record whose destination is not held by an enemy (CCountry::IsEnemy) is counted nowhere. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 13.
